result.target_topic: Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) Requirements and Compliance
result.target_summary: The Corporation must maintain a minimum SLR of 3.0% plus a 2.0% leverage buffer to avoid restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments, with the numerator defined as quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital and the denominator based on total leverage exposure. At December 31, 2024, its insured depository institution subsidiaries exceeded the 6.0% minimum SLR required to be considered well capitalized under the PCA framework.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's Supplementary Leverage Ratio was 5.8% as of December 31, 2024, largely unchanged from the prior year, as higher Tier 1 Capital was offset by an increase in Total Leverage Exposure.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures concern the Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR). While BAC defines the regulatory minimums and compliance thresholds (3.0% plus 2.0% buffer, and 6.0% for well-capitalized status), C provides the specific calculated SLR metric for the period (5.8%), illustrating how the company's capital and leverage exposure positions it relative to such requirements. BAC states its subsidiaries exceeded the 6.0% requirement, implying a compliant status, while C reports a 5.8% ratio, which is below the 6.0% well-capitalized threshold mentioned by BAC but above the minimum requirement.

sentences.text: The Corporation is also required to maintain a minimum supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) of 3.0 percent plus a leverage buffer of 2.0 percent in order to avoid certain restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to executive officers.
At December 31, 2024, our insured depository institution subsidiaries exceeded their requirement to maintain a minimum 6.0 percent SLR to be considered well capitalized under the PCA framework.
December 31, 2024 was 5.8%, largely unchanged from December 31, 2023, as higher Tier 1 Capital was offset by an increase in Total Leverage Exposure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Leverage exposure for TLAC purposes consists of average adjusted total assets and certain off-balance sheet exposures.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the definition of leverage exposure used in capital ratio calculations. BAC defines the denominator of the SLR as 'total leverage exposure' composed of on-balance sheet exposures (less deductions) and off-balance sheet exposures. GS similarly defines 'Leverage exposure' as consisting of 'average adjusted total assets and certain off-balance sheet exposures,' providing parallel structural detail on how the denominator for leverage-based ratios is constructed.

sentences.text: The denominator is total leverage exposure based on the daily average of the sum of on-balance sheet exposures less permitted deductions and the simple average of certain off-balance sheet exposures, as of the end of each month in a quarter.
• Leverage exposure consists of average adjusted total assets and certain off-balance sheet exposures.

comparisons.peer_topic: Supplementary Leverage Ratio Definition and Calculation
comparisons.peer_summary: The Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) is defined as Tier 1 capital divided by total leverage exposure, which includes on-balance sheet assets (net of deductions) and certain off-balance sheet exposures. Under Basel III Advanced approach rules, the minimum SLR is 3.0%, with an additional 2.0% buffer required for certain organizations including the Firm.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures define the Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) components and the associated regulatory buffer requirements. BAC states the minimum SLR is 3.0% plus a 2.0% leverage buffer, with the numerator being quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital. JPM confirms the minimum SLR is 3.0% and that certain organizations like the Firm must hold an additional 2.0% leverage buffer, defining the SLR as Tier 1 capital divided by total leverage exposure. Both explicitly link the 2.0% buffer to the 3.0% minimum for enhanced regulatory entities.

sentences.text: The Corporation is also required to maintain a minimum supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) of 3.0 percent plus a leverage buffer of 2.0 percent in order to avoid certain restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments to executive officers.
The numerator of the SLR is quarter-end Basel 3 Tier 1 capital.
Banking organizations subject to the Basel III Advanced approach are currently required to have a minimum SLR of 3.0%.
Certain banking organizations, including the Firm, are also required to hold an additional 2.0% leverage buffer.
The SLR is defined as Tier 1 capital under Basel III divided by the Firm's total leverage exposure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Leverage-based capital requirements include a minimum Tier 1 leverage ratio of 4%, a minimum Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) of 3%, and an enhanced SLR capital buffer of at least 2%.
